E10_decision_gate.e8_does_not_substitute: E8 (once run) can address only the 'Quality confound' condition on its own separate q-matched construction -- it cannot supply or substitute for the three missing E7-detector-derived conditions above, because E8's own conditions (G-RND-QMATCH/G-DET-QMATCH/G-LLM-QMATCH) are a different comparison than the raw cross-domain/real-only/semantic-ablation comparisons E10 requires
E10_decision_gate.fail_closed_rule: because E7's core synthetic detector conditions (G-RND/G-DET/G-LLM/G-LLM-SHUFFLE-A) are unavailable in every fold, THREE of E10's five required positive-evidence conditions (spec section 17 table) cannot currently be demonstrated: (1) 'Cross-domain signal' -- frozen LLM bank not last on >=2/3 held-out folds by ACER, requires completed E7 G-LLM/G-RND/G-DET trainings; (2) 'Value over real-only' -- LLM better than REAL-ONLY on >=2/3 folds by mean ACER, requires completed E7 G-LLM trainings; (3) 'Semantic ablation' -- LLM-original better than LLM-SHUFFLE-A, requires completed E7 G-LLM and G-LLM-SHUFFLE-A trainings. The remaining two conditions ('Quality confound' and 'Integrity') do not require an E7 detector training and can be assessed via E8 and the BA-controls/threshold-transfer diagnostics respectively
E10_decision_gate.mandatory_interpretation_rule: when E10 is eventually executed, the ABSENCE of the three E7-detector-derived conditions above must NOT be interpreted as, treated as, or silently converted into positive support for E11. The gate must fail closed (resolve to the spec's own explicit fallback: 'do not call the LLM again') unless the frozen specification's required evidence is actually available AND satisfied. No substitute criteria may be invented to route around a missing E7-detector-derived condition
E10_decision_gate.reason: E10 is a DECISION GATE, not a detector experiment -- governing spec Appendix D's Q2-NoLLM execution profile explicitly lists E10 ('E10 decision') as a required step of that profile (no LLM API call), and section 17's purpose is to decide whether calling the LLM again (E11) is justified. A gate can be evaluated -- and can legitimately resolve to its negative branch -- even when some of its positive-evidence inputs are unavailable; the absence of inputs is itself a valid, decidable outcome under the spec's own explicit fallback ('if the above conditions are not met, do NOT call the LLM again')
